Project Description:
The proposed coastal berth at Hangarakatte Karnataka is proposed to be developed along the estuarine region of the Sita River. The land has been acquired in 2009 & 2011 by the State Government of Karnataka to develop the Coastal berth. The proposed construction of a coastal berth facility is for the safe landing of vessels and fisheries boats along with dredging of the approach channel. The harbour is at a distance of about 2.5 km from NH-66. The project is being implemented by the State Port and Fisheries Department, with an estimated cost of Rs. 78.28 Crores.  The proposed coastal berth consists of the following components:
•	Construction of coastal berth of 200.00 mtrs length and 20 mtrs width.
•	Construction of a Backup yard with length 200m and width 60m.
•	Block wall with length 60m and width 4m.
•	Dredging 75 meters wide approach channel including turning radius to an elevation of -6.0 meters for about 1025 meters length from coastal berth to the river mouth in the estuary .

Project Description:
JSW Steel Limited, proposes to set up Iron Ore Beneficiation plant near Taranagar village, Sandur Taluk, Ballari District, Karanataka to beneficiate 25 MTPA of High Siliceous Iron ore (BHQ) to produce 10 MTPA iron ore concentrate. The plant will be set up in two phases of 12.5 MTPA each. 
Low grade iron ore will be received at the plant site from nearby mines through pipe conveyor and / or road. The received material will be screened, crushed and ground with water to the desired size. The iron ore slurry will be routed through cyclones and spiral classifiers to recover high grade ore. The rejects and middlings will be routed through magnetic separators and “Column Reverse Floatation” to recover residual high grade material. The recovered high grade material will be thickened and pumped to JSW Steel Ltd.’s Pellet Plant for production of beneficiated iron ore Pellets. 15 MTPA of tailings will be generated. These will be dewatered and thickened and disposed to tailings disposal area.
Project Name: EC for Setting up of 25 MTPA capacity (mineral throughput) Green-field High Siliceous Iron Ore (BHQ) Beneficiation Plant & associated infrastructure at Taranagar, Sandur, Ballari, Karnataka

Project Description:
The proposed project involves the establishment of a Pre-University College with a Ladies Hostel over an area of 0.950374 hectares of forest land in F. Sy. No. 150A, Sirsi Village, Sirsi Taluk, Uttara Kannada District, by Millat Welfare and Education Trust. The college will provide affordable and accessible higher secondary education, particularly for students from rural and economically weaker families. The proposed Ladies Hostel will provide safe and affordable accommodation for deserving girl students.

The project aims to address the shortage of suitable educational facilities and non-forest land in Sirsi Taluk and improve access to higher secondary education, reduce student dropouts, promote girls’ education, and contribute to the educational and socio-economic development of the region.
Project Name: Proposal for the diversion of forest land in F.Sy.No. 150 of Sirsi Village for the construction of an approach road and Millat Pre-University College, in favor of Millat Welfare and Education Trust, Sirsi.

After considering several alternate forest sites, we selected the current location (F.Sy.No. 150) due to its minimal environmental impact. This site has fewer trees, less vegetation, and hard soil, making it the least disruptive option for the project. This selection ensures minimal harm to the environment while meeting our infrastructure needs.

Project Description:
As per the MoU between IISc and Bandipura Tiger Reserve, (Item 1) “Study of the influence of deep tree roots on water and nutrient cycling in forest and Agro-forestry plots”, and (Item 2) “setting-up of instrumentation and data retrieval for remote sensing study of forest hydrology”,  permission is sought to establish a long term observation pit (Item 1) and a flux tower (Item 2) in the Moolehole catchment, Bandipura tiger reserve.

Detailed description of the research projects:
Item 1,  involves manually digging a pit of 6 to 7m deep maximum, depending on rock hardness, and 150cm diameter, which will be stabilized at the bottom with reinforced concrete. The pit will have several sensors at different levels.

For Item 2, the flux tower is proposed to be built on the same frame as the nearby existing watch tower; however, instead of a shed, the four poles of the tower are extended upwards towards the minimum measurement height for water and carbon gas exchange and associated sensors.

Project Description:
JSW Steel Limited, proposes to set up Iron Ore Beneficiation plant near Taranagar village, Sandur Taluk, Ballari District, Karanataka to beneficiate 25 MTPA of High Siliceous Iron ore (BHQ) to produce 10 MTPA iron ore concentrate. The plant will be set up in two phases of 12.5 MTPA each. 
Low grade iron ore will be received at the plant site from nearby mines through pipe conveyor and / or road. The received material will be screened, crushed and ground with water to the desired size. The iron ore slurry will be routed through cyclones and spiral classifiers to recover high grade ore. The rejects and middlings will be routed through magnetic separators and “Column Reverse Floatation” to recover residual high grade material. The recovered high grade material will be thickened and pumped to JSW Steel Ltd.’s Pellet Plant for production of beneficiated iron ore Pellets. 15 MTPA of tailings will be generated. These will be dewatered and thickened and disposed to tailings disposal area.
Project Name: EC for Setting up of 25 MTPA capacity (mineral throughput) Green-field High Siliceous Iron Ore (BHQ) Beneficiation Plant & associated infrastructure at Taranagar, Sandur, Ballari, Karnataka

Project Description: The proposed Narihalla Pumped Storage Project is an open- loop system. The project envisages construction of upper dam (Gross Capacity 8 MCM). Existing Narihalla Reservoir (Gross Capacity 19.36 MCM) shall be used as lower reservoir. The project contemplates utilization of 5.85 MCM of storage available between RL 530.00 m (MDDL) & RL 542.315 m (FRL) of the Narihalla reservoir without any modifications to the existing Narihalla dam and its appurtenant structures. The water conductor system and powerhouse (2x150MW) shall be totally underground. The one-time water requirement for the initial filling (8MCM) will be pumped from Narihalla reservoir and annual requirement for recuperating losses in reservoir storage is considered only for upper reservoir, which works out to be about 0.46 MCM.
EC Consultant: EQMS Global Pvt. Ltd. formerly known as EQMS India Pvt. Ltd.
